title: The Olympian Gods at Troy
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Mediterranean Travels
description: Predict, then sort the twelve Olympian gods by the side each took in Homer's Iliad: helped the Greeks, helped the Trojans, or stayed above or outside the fight.

educational.topic: The Olympian gods and the Trojan War in Homer's Iliad
learningObjectives: Classify each of the twelve Olympian gods by the side they take in Homer's Iliad (helped the Greeks, helped the Trojans, or stayed above or outside the fight), using each god's domain and story, with at least 10 of 12 correct on the first check.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Prediction followed by a drag-and-drop classification with staged feedback (mark, hint, then reason)
keyQuestions: When the gods went down to the plain of Troy, whose side was each one on?
Which three sides follow from the Judgment of Paris?
Why did the god of war fight for the losing side?
commonMisconceptions: The gods acted as impartial judges of right and wrong.
The god of war must have been on the winning side.
Zeus was simply a Trojan partisan.
assessmentOpportunities: First-check score on twelve cards (mastery: 10 of 12).
Compare the committed prediction of the three totals with the true totals 5, 4, 3.
